title: Orientation and tensor factors for an isomorphism self-square
statement: In the setting of [lem-pur-tower-purity-presentation-retagging], let gX,gY be scheme isomorphisms and let their square with f=jp be Cartesian. Fix the actual tower calculus, exchange laws, constructible-domain witnesses hx,hy, strict normalized root comparison t and Retagging for a. Then the recorded compact-support exchange is invertible. There exists a map u from pullback of the exceptional coefficient unit to that exceptional unit such that: (1) pullback of the orientation followed by u equals orderedRoots(t,d) followed by the orientation; (2) pullback of the tensor transpose followed by the inverse realization comparison and the realization of the specified counit mate equals tensor-pullback comparison, tensor of the pullback-square map with u, then the tensor transpose at P(K). Both identities hold in the ordinary derived tower category, not merely after evaluation. This only asserts the two constituent equations and exchange invertibility; it does not assert the purity square, conjugation, normalization or source naturality.

proof.text: Give source copies the structural maps gX followed by aX and gY followed by aY. The square makes the unchanged f linear; gX,gY are linear to the original copies. Isomorphisms preserve finite-type and separated hypotheses and the underlying smooth morphism keeps its dimension.

Apply tower exceptional base change; its compact-support comparison, followed by the canonical compactification refinement, is the recorded exchange. Its inverse isomorphism follows also from the exchange laws. Compare the returned right adjoint with G by the counit-preserving comparison. Injectivity of the Hom bijection identifies the transported exceptional exchange with the specified counit mate.

Apply the orientation and tensor equations (1) and (2) of tower_factors to that linear square. The assumed Retagging identifies the same-compactification presentations with a. Both twist maps act by restriction on scalar/root generators; hence their strict comparison is t and their ordered powers agree. Let u be the unit exceptional exchange followed by G of the coefficient-unit comparison. This yields the two displayed equations, with quotient transitions retained.
